questions.question: If a sum of money becomes ₹6,000 in 3 years and ₹10,500 in 7 years and 6 months at the same rate of simple interest, then what is the rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: If a sum of money becomes ₹6,000 in 3 years and ₹10,500 in 7 years and 6 months at the same rate of simple interest, then what is the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Sum of money becomes ₹6,000 in 3 years

And ₹10,500 in 7 years and 6 months 

Formula used:

Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100

Where, P is the principal, R is the rate and T is the time.

Calculation:

According to the question,

Simple interest for 4.5 years is = 10500 - 6000 = 4500

Simple interest for 1 years becomes, 4500/4.5 = 1000 

And Simple interest for 3 years = 1000× 3 = 3000

As, we know Total Amount = Simple interest + Principal 

⇒ 6000 = 3000 + Prinicipal

⇒ Prinicipal = 3000 

Using the formula,

⇒ 3000 = (3000 × R × 3 )100

⇒ R = 100/3 = \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\)

∴ The rate of interest is \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\).

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 95 amounts to Rs. 105 in 3 years at a certain rate of simple interest. In 5 years, at the same rate of interest, what will a sum of Rs. 171 amount to:
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 95 amounts to Rs. 105 in 3 years at a certain rate of simple interest. In 5 years, at the same rate of interest, what will a sum of Rs. 171 amount to:
questions.solution:
Given:

A sum of Rs.95 amounts to Rs.105 in 3 years at a certain rate of simple interest. 

Concept used:

Simple interest 

Calculation:

Principal = Rs.95

Amount = Rs.105

Interest = Amount - Principal

Interest = 105 - 95

Interest = Rs. 10

⇒ \({\rm{Si = }}\frac{{{\rm{P }}\ \times\ {\rm{R}} \ \times\ {\rm{T}}}}{{100}}\)

⇒ Rate = \(\frac{{Interest \ \times\ 100}}{{{\rm{Principal\ }} \times\ {\rm{ Time}}}} \)

⇒ Rate = \(\frac{{10 \ \times\ 100}}{{95 \ \times\ 3}}\)

At same rate for a sum of Rs.171 for 5 years

\(\Rightarrow {\rm{Si = }}\frac{{{\rm{P }}\ \times\ {\rm{R}} \ \times\ {\rm{T}}}}{{100}}\)

\(\Rightarrow {\rm{Si = }}\frac{{171 \ \times\ 10 \ \times\ 100\ \times \ 5}}{{95\ \times \ 3 \ \times\ 100}}\)

⇒ Si = 30

Amount = Principal + interest

Amount = 171 + 30

Amount = Rs. 201

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 4 years at 14% per annum is Rs. 6,160 less than the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for 8 years. Find the sum.
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum for 4 years at 14% per annum is Rs. 6,160 less than the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for 8 years. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
Given:

Simple interest for 4 years (SI4) at 14% per annum is ₹6,160 less than simple interest for 8 years (SI8) at the same rate.

Rate (R) = 14%

Time difference (t) = 8 - 4 = 4 years

SI8 - SI4 = ₹6,160

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time

Calculations:

SI8 = (P × 14 × 8) / 100

SI4 = (P × 14 × 4) / 100

SI8 - SI4 = ₹6,160

⇒ [(P × 14 × 8) / 100] - [(P × 14 × 4) / 100] = ₹6,160

⇒ (P × 14 × 4) / 100 = ₹6,160

⇒ (P × 56) / 100 = ₹6,160

⇒ P = (₹6,160 × 100) / 56

⇒ P = ₹11,000

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

Amount = 56

Rate = 16%

Interest = Amount - Principal

Interest = Principal × Rate × Time/100

Calculation- 

Interest = 56 - 24 = 32

According to Question -

Interest = Principal × Rate × Time/100

⇒ 32 = 24 × 16 × Time/100

⇒ Time = 25/3 years

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 5,000 was lent to two people. one at the rate of 16% and the other at the rate of 24%. If the simple interest after one year is Rs. 960. what is the sum lent at the higher rate?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 5,000 was lent to two people. one at the rate of 16% and the other at the rate of 24%. If the simple interest after one year is Rs. 960. what is the sum lent at the higher rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total sum lent = Rs. 5,000

Interest rate for first person = 16%

Interest rate for second person = 24%

Total simple interest after one year = Rs. 960

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time / 100

Calculation:

Let the sum lent at the higher rate (24%) be Rs. x.

Then, the sum lent at the lower rate (16%) = Rs. (5000 - x).

Interest from the higher rate = x × 24 × 1 / 100 = 0.24x

Interest from the lower rate = (5000 - x) × 16 × 1 / 100 = 0.16(5000 - x)

Total interest = 0.24x + 0.16(5000 - x) = 960

⇒ 0.24x + 0.16 × 5000 - 0.16x = 960

⇒ 0.24x + 800 - 0.16x = 960

⇒ 0.08x + 800 = 960

⇒ 0.08x = 960 - 800

⇒ 0.08x = 160

⇒ x = 160 / 0.08

⇒ x = 2000

The sum lent at the higher rate is Rs. 2,000.

questions.question: A person invested a total of Rs. 9,000 in three parts at 3%, 4% and 6% per annum on simple interest. At the end of a year, he received equal interest in all the three cases. The amount invested at 6% is:
questions.questionHtml: A person invested a total of Rs. 9,000 in three parts at 3%, 4% and 6% per annum on simple interest. At the end of a year, he received equal interest in all the three cases. The amount invested at 6% is:
questions.solution:
Given:

principal = Rs. 9,000

Invested in three parts at 3%, 4% and 6% on simple interest 

Formula used:

S.I = (principal × rate × time)/100

Calculation:

Let the amount be x, y, and z respectively.

⇒ s.i = (x × 3 × 1/100) = (y × 4 × 1/100) = (z × 6 × 1/100)

⇒ x : y : z = (1/3) : (1/4) : (1/6)

⇒ x : y : z = 4 : 3 : 2

So, The amount invested at 6% = (2 × 9000/9)

⇒ Rs. 2000

∴ Amount invested at 6% is Rs, 2.000.

questions.question: A sum of ₹10,000 is taken as a loan by Rajesh at a rate of 15% p.a. simple interest for 2 years. But Rajesh could not repay it at the agreed time and asked for an extension of two more years. So, the lender included the interest amount for the period as principal for the next two years at the same rate of interest. The total amount paid by Rajesh at the end of 4 years is: Ans
questions.questionHtml:
A sum of ₹10,000 is taken as a loan by Rajesh at a rate of 15% p.a. simple interest for 2 years. But Rajesh could not repay it at the agreed time and asked for an extension of two more years. So, the lender included the interest amount for the period as principal for the next two years at the same rate of interest. The total amount paid by Rajesh at the end of 4 years is:
Ans
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Simple Interest (SI) percentage for 2 years at 15% p.a. = 15 × 2 = 30%.

Amount after the first 2 years = 10000 × 1.30 = ₹13,000.

The lender includes the interest in the principal, so the new principal for the next 2 years is ₹13,000.

Amount after the next 2 years = 13000 × 1.30 = ₹16,900.

∴ The correct answer is ₹16,900.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Principal (P1) = ₹10,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 15% p.a.

Time period (T1) = 2 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ SI for the first 2 years = (10000 × 15 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹3,000

⇒ Amount at the end of 2 years = 10000 + 3000 = ₹13,000

⇒ The new principal for the next 2 years (P2) = ₹13,000

⇒ SI for the next 2 years = (13000 × 15 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹3,900

⇒ Total amount paid = P2 + SI for the next 2 years = 13000 + 3900 = ₹16,900

∴ The correct answer is ₹16,900.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated uniformly on the initial principal throughout the loan period. The generic formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total amount paid at the end of the term is the sum of the principal and the interest earned. Amount = P + SI.

Compounding Effect in SI

If simple interest is added to the principal midway during an extended period, the subsequent interest is calculated on the new increased principal. This effectively functions like compound interest for the new term block.

questions.solution:
Given:

P1 = 7000, T1 = 3 year, R1 = 5%

P1 = 7000, T2 = 3 year, R2 = 6(1/3)%

Formula used:

Simple interest = (Principal amount × rate of interest × time)/100

Calculation:

S.I.1 = (P1 × R1 × T1)/100

⇒ (7000 × 3 × 5)/100

⇒ 1050

S.I. for one year = 1050/3

⇒ 350

S.I.2 = (P1 × R2 × T2)/10

⇒ [7000 × (19/3) × 3]/100

⇒ 1330

S.I.2 for one year = 1330/3

⇒ 443.33

Gain for one year = 443.33 – 350

⇒ 93.33

∴ His gain in the transaction per year is 93.33

questions.question: A sum at a certain rate of simple interest becomes Rs. 14880 after 3 years and Rs. 16800 after 5 years. Find the simple interest on the same sum at 10% per annum for 4 years (in Rs.).
questions.questionHtml: A sum at a certain rate of simple interest becomes Rs. 14880 after 3 years and Rs. 16800 after 5 years. Find the simple interest on the same sum at 10% per annum for 4 years (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount after 3 years = Rs.14880

Amount after 5 years = Rs.16800

Formula:

Let P = Principal, R = Rate of interest and N = time period

Simple interest = PNR/100

Amount = Principal + SI

Calculation:

Amount for 3 years

⇒ 14880 = PR × 3/100 + P      ----(1)

Amount for 5 years

⇒ 16800 = PR × 5/100 + P      ----(2)

Subtracting eq(1) from eq(2)

2PR/100 = 1920

⇒  PR = 96000

Then,

⇒ 16800 = 96000 × 5/100 + P

⇒ P = 12000

Sum is Rs.12000.

Simple interest = 12000 × 10 × 4/100 = Rs.4800

∴ Simple interest on the same sum at 10% per annum for 4 years is Rs.4800.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 10,200 is invested partly at 8% per annum and remaining at 6% per annum for 3 years at simple interest. If the total interest is Rs. 2,124, how much money was invested at 6% per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 10,200 is invested partly at 8% per annum and remaining at 6% per annum for 3 years at simple interest. If the total interest is Rs. 2,124, how much money was invested at 6% per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total sum, A = Rs 10,200

Rate , R1 = 8% pa

Rate R2 = 6% pa

Time, T = 3 years

Total interest obtained = Rs 2,124

Concept used:

Simple interest, SI = PRT/100

Amount, A = Principal, P + SI

Calculation:

Let the Rs. x invested at 6% per annum.

Money invested at 8% per annum = Rs. (10,200 - x)

Simple interest in 3 years = Rs. 2,124

Simple interest in 1 years = 2,124/3 = Rs. 708

According to the question

x × 6/100 + (10,200 - x) × 8/100 = 708

6x + 81600 - 8x = 708 × 100

8x - 6x = 81600 - 70800 = 10,800

x = 5400

∴ Amount invested at 6% pa is Rs 5400.

questions.question: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 8,928 in two years and to Rs. 10,224 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years, both at simple interest. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 8,928 in two years and to Rs. 10,224 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years, both at simple interest. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount after 2 years = Rs 8928

Amount after 3(1/2) years = Rs 10,224

Concept used:

SI = PRT/100

A = P + SI

P → princiapl R → rate of interest T → time

Calculation:

SI for 3/2 years = amount after 3(1/2) years - amount after 2 years =10224 – 8928 = 1296

SI for 3/2 years  = 1296

SI for 2 years = 1296 × (2/3) × 2 = 1728

Principal = 8928 – 1728 = 7200

R= (100 × SI) / (P × T)

R = (100 × 1728) / (7200 × 2) = 12%

∴ The rate of interest is 12%.

Alternate Method

Amount after 2 years = Rs 8928

Amount after 3(1/2) years = Rs 10,224

⇒ A  = P +2 SI  ------------(1)

⇒ A = P + 7/2SI  -------------(2)

⇒ 3/2 SI = 10224 - 8928

⇒ 3/2 SI = 1296

⇒ SI = (1296 × 2)/3

⇒ SI = Rs. 864

Now,putting value of SI in eq(2) we get.

⇒ P = 10224 - 7/2 × 864

⇒ P = 7200

Rate = Interest(1 year)/Principal 

Rate = 864/7200 × 100

= 12

Rate % = 12 %

questions.question: A certain sum (in Rs.) is invested at simple interest at y% per annum for \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years. Had it been invested at (y + 4)% per annum at simple interest, it would have fetched Rs. 4,452 more as interst. What is the sum?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum (in Rs.) is invested at simple interest at y% per annum for \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years. Had it been invested at (y + 4)% per annum at simple interest, it would have fetched Rs. 4,452 more as interst. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
Short Trick:

Difference of rate for 1 year = 4%

Difference of rate for 3½ year = 4 × 7/2 = 14%

14% = 4452

100% = 4452 × (100/14) = Rs. 31800

Detailed method:

Let sum be Rs x

t = 3½ year

r = 4%

According to the question

Prt/100 = SI

[x × (y + 4 – y) × (7/2)] /100 = 4452

(x × 4 × 7)/(2 × 100) = 4452

x = (4452 × 2 × 100)/(4 × 7)

x = Rs. 31800

questions.solution: \(\frac{\frac{1}{2}x × 20 × 2}{100} + \frac{\frac{1}{5}x × 25 × 2}{100} + \frac{\frac{3}{10}x × 10 × 2}{100} = 360 \)  ⇒ 20x + 10x + 6x = 360 × 100 ⇒ 36x = 36000 ⇒ x = 1000

questions.question: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 1,860 in 2 years and to Rs. 2,130 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years at simple interest. Find the sum and the rate of interest, respectively.
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 1,860 in 2 years and to Rs. 2,130 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years at simple interest. Find the sum and the rate of interest, respectively.
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 1,860 in 2 years and to Rs. 2,130 in 31⁄2 years at simple interest.

Concept:

Simple Interest (SI) is calculated using the formula:
SI = Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T) / 100

Amount (A) is given by:
A = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Calculation:

Let the principal be P and the rate of interest be R%.

For the first condition:

⇒ A1 = P + (P × R × 2 / 100) = 1860

⇒ P (1 + 2R / 100) = 1860     ...(i)

For the second condition:

⇒ A2 = P + (P × R × 3.5 / 100) = 2130

⇒ P (1 + 3.5R / 100) = 2130     ...(ii)

From equation (i):

⇒ P (1 + 2R / 100) = 1860

⇒ P = 1860 / (1 + 2R / 100)     ...(iii)

Substitute P from equation (iii) into equation (ii):

⇒ (1860 / (1 + 2R / 100)) × (1 + 3.5R / 100) = 2130

⇒ 1860 (1 + 3.5R / 100) = 2130 (1 + 2R / 100)

⇒ 1860 + 1860 × 3.5R / 100 = 2130 + 2130 × 2R / 100

⇒ 1860 + 65.1R = 2130 + 42.6R

⇒ 22.5R = 270

⇒ R = 270 / 22.5

⇒ R = 12%

Substitute R = 12% back into equation (iii) to find P:

⇒ P = 1860 / (1 + 2 × 12 / 100)

⇒ P = 1860 / 1.24

⇒ P = 1500

∴ The sum is Rs. 1,500 and the rate of interest is 12%.

questions.question: In what time will ₹3,720 amount to ₹5,282.4 at 12% simple interest per annum?
questions.questionHtml: In what time will ₹3,720 amount to ₹5,282.4 at 12% simple interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

The simple interest = 5282.4 - 3720 = 1562.4

⇒ \(1562.4={3720\ × 12\ × T\over100}\)

⇒ T = 3.5 years

∴ The required result will be 3.5 years.

questions.question: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at the rate of 4% per annum is Rs. 76, then what is the sum?
questions.questionHtml: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at the rate of 4% per annum is Rs. 76, then what is the sum?
questions.solution:
Let the sum be Rs. 100%

Simple interest = (4% × 3) = 12%

Compounded interest 

⇒ 4% + 4% + (16/100)% = 8.16%

⇒ 8.16% + 4% + (8.16 × 4)/100 = 12.4864%

⇒ 12.4864% - 12% → 76 ⇒ 0.4864% → 76 ⇒ 1% → 76/0.4864 = 156.25 ⇒ 100% → 15625

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 36,000 is divided into two parts, A and B, such that the simple interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on A and B after two years and four years, respectively, is equal. The total interest (in Rs.) received from A is:
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 36,000 is divided into two parts, A and B, such that the simple interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on A and B after two years and four years, respectively, is equal. The total interest (in Rs.) received from A is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 36,000

Rate of interest = 15%

Time for A and B = 2 years and 4 years respectively

Formula used:

Simple interest = (principal × rate × time)/100

Calculation:

Let Principle for A be Rs. X

Then principal for B = 36,000 - X

Simple interest for A = (X × 15 × 2)/100

⇒ 30X/100

⇒ 0.3X

Simple interest for B = [(36,000 – X) × 15 × 4]/100

⇒ 0.6 × (36,000 – X)

⇒ 21600 – 0.6X

Now, simple interest of A in 2 years = simple interest for B in 4 years.

0.3X = 21600 – 0.6X

⇒ 0.3X + 0.6X = 21600

⇒ 0.9X = 21600

⇒ X = 21600/0.9

⇒ X = 24000

Then simple interest of A in two years = 0.3X

⇒ 0.3 × 24000

⇒ 7200

∴ The simple interest of A is Rs. 7200.

questions.question: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 9,766 in 3 years at simple interest at R% per annum and to Rs. 10,849 in \(4\frac{1}{2}\) years at the same rate of simple interest. The value of R is:
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 9,766 in 3 years at simple interest at R% per annum and to Rs. 10,849 in \(4\frac{1}{2}\) years at the same rate of simple interest. The value of R is:
questions.solution:
Given

Amount in 3 years = Rs. 9766

Amount in \(4{1\over2}\) years = Rs. 10,849

Formula used

Simple interest = (P × R × T)/100

where P, R and T are principal, rate and time.

Calculation

Amount = Principal + simple interest

9766 = Principal + simple interest for 3 years      ---- (1)

10,849 = Principal + simple interest for 4.5 years       ---- (2)

subtract (1) from (2)

Simple interest for 1.5 years = 10,849 - 9766 = Rs. 1083

Simple interest for 1 years = Rs.1083/1.5 = Rs 722

Simple interest for 3 years = Rs 722 × 3 = Rs. 2166

Principal = Amount - Simple interest

⇒ Rs. 9766 - Rs 2166

⇒ Rs. 7600

Now,

⇒ (P × R × T)/100 = S.I

⇒ (7600 × R × 3)/100 = 2166

⇒ R = (2166 × 100)/(7600 × 3)

⇒ R = 9.5 %

∴ The value of R is 9.5%

questions.question: A sum of ₹16,875 was lent out at simple interest, and at the end of 1 year 8 months, the total amount was ₹18,000. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.questionHtml: A sum of ₹16,875 was lent out at simple interest, and at the end of 1 year 8 months, the total amount was ₹18,000. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
Given:

The sum of lent out at simple interest = 16,875

The amount = 18000

The time = 1 year 8 months

Formula used:

\(S.I={P× R× T\over100}\)     Where, S.I. = Simple interest, P = Principle, R = Rate, and T = Time

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest R

The simple interest = 18000 - 16875 = 1125

Time =  \(({1+{8\over12}})=({1+{2\over3}})=({3+2\over3})={5\over3}\)

⇒ \({1125}={{16875\ × R× {5\over3}}\over100}\)

⇒ 1125 × 100 = 16875 × R × \({5\over3}\)

⇒ 112500 = 28125R

⇒ R = \({ 112500\over28125}\) = 4%

∴ The required result will be 4%.

questions.question: A sum of money invested at a certain rate of simple interest per annum amounts to Rs. 14,522 in seven years and to Rs. 18,906 in eleven years. Find the sum invested (in Rs.).
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money invested at a certain rate of simple interest per annum amounts to Rs. 14,522 in seven years and to Rs. 18,906 in eleven years. Find the sum invested (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
Amount produce in 7 years = Rs.14522 ; Amount produce in 11 years = Rs.18906

S.I produced in (11 - 7) = 4 years = (18906 - 14522) = Rs.4384 ⇒ S.I in 1 years = 4384/4 = 1096

Principal = 14522 - (1096 × 7) ⇒ (14522 - 7672) = Rs.6850

questions.question: A person borrowed 1,200 at 8% p.a. and Rs. 1,800 at 10% p.a. as simple interest for the same period. He has to pay Rs. 1,380 in all as interest. Find the time period.
questions.questionHtml: A person borrowed 1,200 at 8% p.a. and Rs. 1,800 at 10% p.a. as simple interest for the same period. He has to pay Rs. 1,380 in all as interest. Find the time period.
questions.solution:
Given :

A person borrowed 1,200 at 8% p.a. and Rs. 1,800 at 10% p.a. as simple interest for the same period. He has to pay Rs. 1,380 in all as interest.

Concept used :

Interest = (Principle × Rate of interest × time)/100 

Calculation: 

Let the time period be 't' years 

Interest for Rs. 1200 at 8% rate of interest = (1200 × 8 × t)/100 = 96t 

Interest for Rs. 1800 at 10% rate of interest = (1800 × 10 × t)/100 = 180t 

Total interest = 1380 

⇒ 96t + 180t = 1380 

⇒ 276t = 1380 

⇒ t = 5 years. 

∴ Option 4 will be the correct answer.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 15,000 is invested partly at 12% per annum and the remaining at 10% per annum simple interest. If the total interest at end of 2 years is Rs. 3,344 how much money was invested at 10% per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 15,000 is invested partly at 12% per annum and the remaining at 10% per annum simple interest. If the total interest at end of 2 years is Rs. 3,344 how much money was invested at 10% per annum?
questions.solution:
Let Rs. x invested at 12% per annum and (15000 - x) invested at 10% per annum

\(\frac{{x \times 2 \times 12\;}}{{100}} + \frac{{\left( {15000 - x} \right) \times 10 \times 2}}{{100\;}} = 3344\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{12x}}{{100}} + \frac{{150000 - 10x}}{{100}} = 1672\)

⇒ 2x + 150000 = 167200

∴ x = 8600

Money invested at 10% per annum = 15000 - 8600 = Rs. 6400

questions.question: R wants to deposit ₹80,000 in the bank for a year. In his account, the bank gives 12% simple annual interest but charges ₹3,000 as a processing fee for the account. What would be his percentage earnings in the account?
questions.questionHtml: R wants to deposit ₹80,000 in the bank for a year. In his account, the bank gives 12% simple annual interest but charges ₹3,000 as a processing fee for the account. What would be his percentage earnings in the account?
questions.solution:
Simple interest is  80000 × 12 × 1/100 = Rs 9600

After charging the processing fee the profit amount 9600 - 3000 = 6600

 The percentage of earning in this account is (6600 / 80000) × 100 = 8.25%

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 12,800 is invested partly at 15% per annum and the remaining at 12% per annum simple interest. If the total interest at end of 3 years is Rs. 5,085, then how much money was invested at 15% per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 12,800 is invested partly at 15% per annum and the remaining at 12% per annum simple interest. If the total interest at end of 3 years is Rs. 5,085, then how much money was invested at 15% per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total amount = Rs. 12800

Partly at 15% per annum and the remaining at 12% per annum simple

interest.

Interest at end of 3 years is Rs. 5,085

Formula used:

SI = (P × T × R)/100

Where P = principal , T = time and R = rate of interest. 

Calculation:

Let Rs. y invested at 15% per annum.

Money invested at 12% per annum = Rs. (12,800 - y)

Simple interest in 3 years = Rs. 5,085

Simple interest in 1 years = 5,085/3 = Rs. 1,695

Using the formula, 

SI = (P × T × R)/100,  for 1 year

⇒ y × 15/100 + (12,800 - y) × 12/100 = 1695

⇒ 15y + 12800 × 12 - 12y = 1695 × 100

⇒ 3y = 169500 - 153600 = 15900

⇒ y = 15900/3 = Rs. 5300

∴ Money was invested at 15% per annum is Rs. 5300.

questions.question: A man borrowed Rs. 29,000 for 3 years and Rs. 45,000 for 5 years at the same rate of simple interest. If he paid a total interest of Rs. 62,400, then what was the rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A man borrowed Rs. 29,000 for 3 years and Rs. 45,000 for 5 years at the same rate of simple interest. If he paid a total interest of Rs. 62,400, then what was the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal1 (P1) = ₹29,000

Time1 (t1) = 3 years

Principal2 (P2) = ₹45,000

Time2 (t2) = 5 years

Total Interest (I) = ₹62,400

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Total Interest = SI1 + SI2

Where, r = rate of interest

Calculation:

SI1 = P1 × r × t1 / 100

SI2 = P2 × r × t2 / 100

Total Interest = SI1 + SI2

62,400 = (29,000 × r × 3 / 100) + (45,000 × r × 5 / 100)

⇒ 62,400 = (87,000r / 100) + (225,000r / 100)

⇒ 62,400 = (87,000r + 225,000r) / 100

⇒ 62,400 = 312,000r / 100

⇒ 62,400 = 3,120r

⇒ r = 62,400 / 3,120

⇒ r = 20%

∴ The correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Simple interest on Rs. 986 for a certain period is Rs. 62 less than simple interest on Rs. 1,296 for the same period at the rate of 5% simple interest. For how many years was each amount invested?
questions.questionHtml: Simple interest on Rs. 986 for a certain period is Rs. 62 less than simple interest on Rs. 1,296 for the same period at the rate of 5% simple interest. For how many years was each amount invested?
questions.solution:
Let the time = T years

As per the question,

​⇒ 1296 × 5 × T / 100 -  986 × 5 × T / 100 = 62

⇒ 310 × 5 T = 6200 ⇒ T = 4 years

questions.question: Aman invested a sum of money in scheme A at the rate of 8% p.a. for a period of 5 years on simple interest. He invested four times of the sum of scheme A in scheme B at the rate of 5% p.a. for 7 years on simple interest. He received a total interest amount of ₹1,620. How much (in ₹) did he invest in scheme B?
questions.questionHtml: Aman invested a sum of money in scheme A at the rate of 8% p.a. for a period of 5 years on simple interest. He invested four times of the sum of scheme A in scheme B at the rate of 5% p.a. for 7 years on simple interest. He received a total interest amount of ₹1,620. How much (in ₹) did he invest in scheme B?
questions.solution:
SIA = x × 8 × 5 / 100 = 0.4x, SIB = 4x × 5 × 7 / 100 = 1.4x

0.4x + 1.4x = 1620, x = 1620 / 1.8 = 900

Amount in scheme B = 4 × 900 = 3600

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 7,656 in 4 years and to Rs. 8,120 in 5 years at a certain simple interest rate per cent per annum. The rate of interest is:
questions.questionHtml: A sum amounts to Rs. 7,656 in 4 years and to Rs. 8,120 in 5 years at a certain simple interest rate per cent per annum. The rate of interest is:
questions.solution:
Interest for 1 year = 8120 - 7656 = 464.

Interest for 4 year = 464 × 4 = 1856.

Principle = 7656 - 1856  = 5800.

464 = (5800 × r × 1)/100

r = 464/58 = 8%
